value.rationale: Particle coincidence absorption on all-to-all networks is a natural nonrectangular multi-detector problem. The full observable projector and its rank are solved for an infinite family, showing a universal 1/n localization jump at equal-rate resonance and an exchange-selective response: symmetric inputs preserve 2/(n-1), while antisymmetric inputs switch between 0 and 2/n. This distinguishes physically motivated state preparations and is not merely numerical, a graph relabelling of a previous rectangle result, or a general method restatement. The n>=4 range excludes the triangle that is already a cycle.
